title: What procedure is to be followed in case of transfer of interest of a member in a company not having share capital?Ans. Section 56 of the Companies Act, 2013 provides that a proper instrument of transfer is required to be executed in case of transfer of the interest of a member in case of a company having no share capital. Such instrument is required to be executed by or on behalf of the transferor and the transferee and must be delivered to the company in terms of the said provision.Rule 11 of the Companies (Share Capital and Debentures) Rules, 2014 provides that form SH-4 shall be the format for transfer of securities held in the physical form. Rule 11(2) of the said rules clarifies that the same form is also required to be used in case of transfer of interest of a member in a company not having Share capital. The said provision clarifies that the reference to securities shall be read as reference tointerest of the member of the company.Accordingly, stakeholders are advised to use form SH-4 for transfer of interest of member in case of a company limited with guarantee in terms of rule 11(2).

title:
Stakeholders are informed that MCA portal will not be available from 15th February 2026 12:00 AM to 15th February 11:59 PM due to establishment of new RDs and ROCs which are effective from 16th February 2026. 
To facilitate implementation of this change, stakeholders are advised to note the following points:
(1)	All registered companies and LLPs mapped with the below mentioned ROC locations currently will be bifurcated as:
a.	ROC Delhi: Companies or LLPs registered with Haryana State will be moved to ROC Haryana and the remaining companies will be split between ROC Delhi I and ROC Delhi II based on existing district and PIN code.
b.	ROC Kanpur: Companies or LLPs registered will be split between ROC Uttar Pradesh I and ROC Uttar Pradesh II based on existing district and PIN code.
c.	ROC Mumbai: Companies or LLPs registered will be split between ROC Mumbai I, ROC Mumbai II and ROC Nagpur based on existing district and PIN code.
d.	ROC Kolkata: Companies or LLPs registered will be split between ROC Kolkata I and ROC Kolkata II based on existing district and PIN code.
(2)	ROC and RD mapping will get updated for all the new RD locations and existing impacted RD locations.
(3)	Please refer Act & Rules - Notifications tab to access the relevant notifications issued on 23rd October 2025.
(4)	All Foreign companies who have their place of business in India will be mapped from ROC Delhi to ROC Delhi I.
(5)	Stakeholders are advised to plan and file/resubmit current V3 forms before 15th February 2026 if the due date/resubmission date falls on 15th February 2026.

title: Form AOC-4 - Filing of Financial Statements
full_text:
Form Name: AOC-4 (Financial Statements)
Purpose: Filing financial statements, balance sheets, profit & loss statements, and director reports.
Who should file: All registered companies under the Companies Act 2013.
Due Date: Within 30 days from the date of the Annual General Meeting (AGM).
Required Documents: Balance Sheet, Profit and Loss Account, Director's Report, Auditor's Report, Notice of AGM.
Penalty: ₹100 per day of delay.
Official Instructions: Must be audited by a chartered accountant and submitted with digital signatures.

title: Form MGT-7 - Annual Return of Company
full_text:
Form Name: MGT-7 (Annual Return)
Purpose: Annual disclosure of shareholding structure, transfers, management, and board meetings.
Who should file: All registered companies (excluding OPCs and small companies who file MGT-7A).
Due Date: Within 60 days from the date of the AGM.
Required Documents: List of shareholders, share transfers list, MGT-8 certificate (for listed/large companies).
Penalty: ₹100 per day of delay.
Official Instructions: Must be digitally signed by a Director and a practicing Company Secretary.

title: Form MGT-14 - Filing of Board/General Meeting Resolutions
full_text:
Form Name: MGT-14 (Filing of Resolutions)
Purpose: Registration of board resolutions or special resolutions passed by shareholders.
Who should file: Companies executing resolutions under Section 117 of the Companies Act 2013.
Due Date: Within 30 days of passing the resolution.
Required Documents: Copy of resolution, explanatory statement, amended Memorandum/Articles (if applicable).
Penalty: Late filing fees (₹100/day); company/directors are subject to default compounding.
Official Instructions: File online on the MCA V3 portal with digital signature authorization.

title: Form DIR-3 KYC - Director Verification and KYC
full_text:
Form Name: DIR-3 KYC (Director KYC)
Purpose: Annual verification of Director Identification Number (DIN) details to keep it active.
Who should file: Every individual holding a DIN as of 31st March of the financial year.
Due Date: On or before 30th September of every financial year.
Required Documents: PAN Card, Aadhaar Card, Passport/Voter ID (identity proof), utility bills (address proof).
Penalty: DIN deactivation and ₹5,000 fine for late reactivation.
Official Instructions: Ensure name, address, and mobile number match identity proofs exactly.

title: Form ADT-1 - Appointment of Auditor
full_text:
Form Name: ADT-1 (Auditor Appointment)
Purpose: Informing the Registrar of the appointment of a new/renewed statutory auditor.
Who should file: Every company appointing an auditor under Section 139.
Due Date: Within 15 days from the date of the AGM where the auditor was appointed.
Required Documents: Auditor consent letter, eligibility certificate, copy of AGM resolution.
Penalty: ₹100 per day of delay.
Official Instructions: File using digital signatures on the web-based MCA V3 portal.

title: Form INC-20A - Declaration of Commencement of Business
full_text:
Form Name: INC-20A (Commencement of Business)
Purpose: Declaring that subscribers to the MOA have paid the value of shares and capital receipt.
Who should file: Companies incorporated after 2nd November 2018 having a share capital.
Due Date: Within 180 days of the date of incorporation.
Required Documents: Bank statement showing receipt of share capital, proof of regulatory approval (if applicable).
Penalty: ₹50,000 for company, ₹1,000/day for directors; company striking-off threat after 180 days.
Official Instructions: File before executing any commercial transactions or borrowing capital.

title: Form PAS-3 - Return of Allotment of Shares
full_text:
Form Name: PAS-3 (Return of Allotment)
Purpose: Registering the allotment of shares or securities issued to public/private investors.
Who should file: All companies allotting shares under Section 39.
Due Date: Within 30 days from the date of allotment.
Required Documents: Board resolution authorizing allotment, list of allottees, valuation report (if non-cash).
Penalty: ₹100 per day of delay.
Official Instructions: File details of nominal value, premium, and date of allocation of shares.

title: Form SH-7 - Alteration of Share Capital
full_text:
Form Name: SH-7 (Alteration of Share Capital)
Purpose: Registering changes/increase in authorized share capital or number of members.
Who should file: Companies increasing or altering their capital structure under Section 64.
Due Date: Within 30 days of passing the resolution.
Required Documents: Resolution copy, altered Memorandum of Association (MOA), altered Articles (AOA).
Penalty: ₹100 per day of delay.
Official Instructions: Upload altered MOA showing the updated capital clause.

title: Form CHG-1 & CHG-4 - Charge Management (Creation & Satisfaction)
full_text:
Form Name: CHG-1 (Charge Creation/Modification) & CHG-4 (Satisfaction of Charge)
Purpose: Registering the creation, modification (CHG-1) or satisfaction (CHG-4) of mortgage/charges.
Who should file: Companies securing bank loans or clearing corporate loan pledges.
Due Date: CHG-1 within 30 days of creation/modification; CHG-4 within 30 days of satisfaction.
Required Documents: Charge/pledge deed, loan agreement, NOC from lender/bank (for CHG-4).
Penalty: Late fees apply; delay beyond 120 days requires Regional Director condonation.
Official Instructions: Check indexing of charges on the MCA portal post-approval.

title: LLP Forms - LLP Form 3 (Agreement), Form 11 (Annual Return) & Form 8 (Solvency)
full_text:
Form Name: LLP Form-3 (LLP Agreement), Form-11 (Annual Return), Form-8 (Accounts & Solvency)
Purpose: Registering LLP agreement (Form 3), submitting yearly returns (Form 11), and financial details (Form 8).
Who should file: All registered Limited Liability Partnerships.
Due Date: Form 11 within 60 days of FY end (30th May); Form 8 within 30 days of end of 6 months of FY (30th October).
Required Documents: Copy of LLP agreement (Form 3), Statement of assets and liabilities (Form 8).
Penalty: ₹100 per day of delay per form.
Official Instructions: Pre-fill partner details using LLPIN prior to submitting.

title: FAQ: What is DIR-3 KYC?
full_text:
Question: What is DIR-3 KYC?
Answer: DIR-3 KYC is an annual verification form that every individual holding a Director Identification Number (DIN) must submit to the Ministry of Corporate Affairs (MCA) to verify and keep their KYC details (identity, contact details, and address) active.

title: FAQ: When should Form AOC-4 be filed?
full_text:
Question: When should Form AOC-4 be filed?
Answer: Form AOC-4 (for filing financial statements) must be filed with the Registrar of Companies (ROC) within 30 days of the date of the company's Annual General Meeting (AGM). For One Person Companies (OPC), it must be filed within 180 days from the closure of the financial year.

title: FAQ: What is the penalty for late filing of DIR-3 KYC?
full_text:
Question: What is the penalty for late filing of DIR-3 KYC?
Answer: If a director fails to file DIR-3 KYC by the due date (30th September), their Director Identification Number (DIN) will be deactivated. A penalty fee of ₹5,000 is required to reactivate the DIN in the system.

title: FAQ: What is the penalty for late filing of Form AOC-4 or MGT-7?
full_text:
Question: What is the penalty for late filing of Form AOC-4 or MGT-7?
Answer: The late filing fee for both Form AOC-4 and Form MGT-7 is ₹100 per day of delay from the respective due date, without any upper limit on the accumulated late fees.

title: FAQ: When should Form MGT-7 be filed?
full_text:
Question: When should Form MGT-7 be filed?
Answer: Form MGT-7 (for filing the company's annual return) must be filed within 60 days of the date on which the Annual General Meeting (AGM) was held or should have been held.

title: FAQ: What is the purpose and due date of Form INC-20A?
full_text:
Question: What is the purpose and due date of Form INC-20A?
Answer: Form INC-20A is the declaration of commencement of business. Every company incorporated with share capital after 2nd November 2018 must file it within 180 days of incorporation to declare that subscribers have paid the value of shares taken. Failure to file incurs a penalty of ₹50,000 and restricts business transactions.

title: FAQ: What are the due dates for LLP Form 11 and LLP Form 8?
full_text:
Question: What are the due dates for LLP Form 11 and LLP Form 8?
Answer: LLP Form 11 (Annual Return) must be filed annually within 60 days from the closure of the financial year (by 30th May). LLP Form 8 (Statement of Accounts & Solvency) must be filed annually within 30 days from the end of 6 months of the financial year (by 30th October).

title: FAQ: What is Form ADT-1 and when must it be filed?
full_text:
Question: What is Form ADT-1 and when must it be filed?
Answer: Form ADT-1 is used by a company to notify the Registrar of Companies (ROC) about the appointment of its statutory auditor. It must be filed within 15 days of the date of the AGM where the auditor was appointed.

title: FAQ: What is the difference between Form MGT-7 and MGT-7A?
full_text:
Question: What is the difference between Form MGT-7 and MGT-7A?
Answer: Form MGT-7 is the standard annual return form for all public and private companies. Form MGT-7A is an abridged annual return form designed specifically for One Person Companies (OPCs) and Small Companies to simplify compliance requirements.
